items.title: [Feature]: support GLM-5.2 ShareIndex with custom VPP layouts
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Background

GLM-5.2 ShareIndex training needs custom virtual pipeline parallelism with uneven decoder-layer placement. `--num-layer-list` is the existing non-VPP uneven-PP distribution mode, while `--pipeline-model-parallel-layout` is the MindSpeed layout mode that fully describes PP/VPP chunks, embedding, decoder, and loss placement. The two arguments are alternative layer-distribution modes and must not be configured together. Runtime and checkpoint conversion must derive the same PP/VPP-to-global-layer mapping from the layout alone.

### Expected implementation

1. Treat `--num-layer-list` and `--pipeline-model-parallel-layout` as mutually exclusive alternatives at training, checkpoint restore, and conversion boundaries.
2. Reuse MindSpeed `PipelineParallelLayerLayout` to validate the custom layout and resolve decoder-layer counts and global offsets for every PP/VPP chunk.
3. Ensure every ShareIndex layer resolves the intended compute source without crossing a process-local PP/VPP boundary.
4. Build and load the correct number of VPP model chunks, persist the layout in checkpoint arguments, and reject conflicting command-line/checkpoint distribution modes.
5. Support custom-layout HF-to-MCore and MCore-to-HF conversion while remaining compatible with Megatron Core v0.12.1.

### Acceptance criteria

- `--pipeline-model-parallel-layout 'Ett|(tttt|)*18ttttL'` alone produces 78 unique global decoder layers across PP=4 and VPP=5.
- Supplying `--num-layer-list` and `--pipeline-model-parallel-layout` together fails with an explicit mutual-exclusion error.
- Each ShareIndex consumer resolves the expected compute source within the same local PP/VPP chunk, with explicit validation errors for invalid split boundaries.
- HF/MCore conversion uses the same layout mapping in both directions, and the resulting VPP checkpoint can be loaded with the configured layout.
- The PR remains a single review commit and the repository checks for the changed-file scope are reported fact

items.title: [Feature Request] Support SAO-style single-rollout asynchronous optimization for agentic RL
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation
GRPO's group-wise sampling seems mismatched with asynchronous agentic RL — the group must wait for the slowest rollout, causing stale data and off-policy drift (the SAO paper reports collapse at ~160 async steps).
SAO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07508) (Tsinghua/GLM team, deployed in GLM-5.2 750B) addresses this with one rollout per prompt + critic, achieving stable training for ~1000 steps and +6 points on SWE-Bench Verified over stabilized GRPO.
I'm wondering if the team would consider supporting this paradigm in verl?
### What SAO does
1. Single-rollout (group size=1): each trajectory trains immediately, no group barrier
2. DIS clipping: use π_rollout directly (drop π_θ_old), mask tokens outside [1-ε_ℓ, 1+ε_h] entirely
3. Faster + frozen-attention critic: K=2 critic updates per policy update; freeze attention layers (only train MoE/MLP)
4. Skip-observation GAE: skip env observation tokens in advantage computation, link action-end → next-action-start

items.title: [rollout, perf] fix: cache the generation-prompt delta in incremental tokenization
items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #7617. `tokenize_non_assistant_incremental_messages()` rendered the full conversation twice after every appended tool/user/system group, only to obtain the tokens that `add_generation_prompt=True` adds. Over a long tool loop that is a quadratic amount of chat-template rendering; the issue measured it at ~34% of rollout wall time on a 200-turn Qwen3.5-9B agent loop.

Following the discussion on the issue (@gxlvera, @wuxibin89): the generation-prompt delta is now **cached on the builder by default**, keyed by the role of the final message and the tool schemas, and filled by the existing full-history render. Builders keep template-specific behaviour through an override hook.

items.title: [Bug][DCP] NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 fused attention bypasses DCP handling
items.bodyExcerpt:
# [Bug][DCP] DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 fused attention bypasses pure-DCP handling

## Problem

The fused DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 path still has two pure-DCP correctness
defects:

1. `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/common/kernels.py` checks owner-local KV slot
   validity before query RMSNorm. A negative slot means another DCP rank owns
   the token's KV entry; it does not remove this rank's query contribution.
2. `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py` gathers query heads and combines
   partial output/LSE only for PCP+DCP. Pure DCP therefore sends rank-local
   query heads into attention over owner-local KV and never performs the
   required cross-rank result merge.

The sparse-indexer DCP rank, world-size, and interleave plumbing mentioned in
the original report has landed independently on `main`; it is no longer part
of this issue.

## Observable regression

A focused kernel reproducer uses an all-negative slot mapping, representing a
DCP rank that owns no KV-cache slot for those tokens.

Expected:

- Query output matches reference RMSNorm.
- MLA and indexer KV caches remain unchanged.
- The Top-K buffer is cleared.

Actual on unpatched `main`:

- Query output remains zero because the kernel returns before query RMSNorm.

At model level, @drakosha reproduced repeated-token output on unpatched
GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with TP4/DCP4 and `fp8_ds_mla`. The patched path produced output
byte-identical to DCP1 for the tested deterministic greedy request.

## Expected behavior

- Query RMSNorm runs independently of owner-local KV-slot validity.
- Negative slots continue to suppress MLA and indexer KV-cache writes.
- Pure DCP gathers query heads before owner-local sparse attention.
- Partial output/LSE is combined across DCP ranks through the existing DCP
  manager.

## Proposed fix and validation

PR #50005 implements the fix and regression coverage.

At its current head:

- The focused fused norm/RoPE suite passes all 67 tests on GB200.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks pass.

### Summary

On ROCm with GLM-5.3-Flash, vLLM logs at startup:

```
Fused multi-step draft decode is not supported by attention backend(s)
DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER, KPOOL_TAIL, ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE;
falling back to rebuilding attention metadata between draft steps.
```

Because the metadata is rebuilt between every draft step, the per-step cost of MTP speculation is high enough that deeper speculation stops paying for itself well before the draft quality runs out. Measurements below quantify the gap.

### Measurements

8x MI350X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, TP8, GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, `--max-model-len 1048576`, 2 000-token context, 256 output tokens, unique per-request prefixes (nothing hits the prefix cache), warmup round then median of 3-4 rounds.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2.57 | 78.4 % | 155 tok/s | 1 432 | 3 012 |
| **4** | **3.36** | 58.9 % | **173** | **1 499** | **3 055** |

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`build_offloading_config` asserts `tokens_per_block % tokens_per_hash == 0` for every KV cache group, so a hybrid model with any group whose blocks are *smaller* than a hash unit cannot enable the OffloadingConnector at all. group[1]   UniformType    4 tok  (indexer tail_cache, 11 layers)   <- rejected
```
group[2-5] MambaSpec   3584 tok  (KDA state, align mode)
group[6]   UniformType   64 tok  (DFlash2 drafter)
tokens_per_hash = 64
```

items.bodyExcerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Some hybrid-model KV groups hold *recent-window state* rather than restorable prefix state. GLM-5.3-Flash's 4-token DSA-indexer `tail_cache` keeps only a live window, which breaks the OffloadingConnector three independent ways:

1. Its engine-side block table is much shorter than `cdiv(hit_tokens, block_size)`, so `update_state_after_alloc` dies on `assert len(group_blocks) >= num_gpu_blocks` for any external hit that includes the group.
2. SWA-style store selection always lands on null placeholder blocks — the group can never store a chunk.
3. Any lookup chain that includes it collapses the min-across-groups hit window to zero — so one such group makes the **whole model** un-restorable even when every other group's chunks are stored and hit.

Related: #52771 / #52735 diagnose the adjacent all-groups-drafter-fallback defect under MTP/EAGLE (which we also hit); this issue is about groups that are *architecturally* unrestorable rather than volatile-tail handling.

### Proposed change (running in production)

Three cooperating hooks (config-driven in our deployment, `kv_connector_extra_config`):

- `load_skip_groups`: the group contributes an empty entry to load specs (workers already skip zero-size groups), so its short block table never trips the allocation assert;
- manager-level **always-hit / never-store** for those groups, so they neither gate nor pollute the hit window;
- `hit_rollback_tokens`: report one mamba-align segment (3,584 tokens here) fewer hit tokens, so the engine **recomputes** the trailing segment — which honestly rebuilds tail/conv/drafter state from the restored KV. Correctness verified by needle-in-context checks across 30/30 restore tests, including 10 simultaneous restores after a full engine restart.

items.bodyExcerpt:
### Bug half

`SharedOffloadRegion` is one mmap file with a slot per rank. On a multi-node engine (mp executor with `--nnodes 2`, ranks on different hosts) the remote rank's slot is never written and startup dies after a multi-minute opaque wait:

```
TimeoutError: Timed out waiting for mmap file to reach 4144029696 bytes
```

`TieringOffloadingSpec` cannot avoid it: it overrides `_uses_shared_region → True` because the scheduler-side StoreController pushes L1 bytes to secondary tiers through a whole-region memoryview — single-host by construction. Plain `CPUOffloadingSpec` could fall back to private pinned tensors (which work fine multi-node), but has no gate either.

**Suggested minimal fix:** detect ranks-per-host at spec init and fail fast with an explicit "multi-node engines are not supported by the shared-region CPU tier" (or fall back to private tensors for the non-tiering spec). Related lifecycle work: #51317 / #52596 (leaked/unlinked regions — we added supporting evidence there from unified-memory hardware, where leaked regions silently shrink the next boot's profiled memory).

### Feature half: node-local tier for multi-node engines

For multi-node engines we built a working alternative worth considering in-tree: a spec where the scheduler keeps **metadata only** (persistent key index; per-key file paths derived from block hashes) and **each rank performs its own disk I/O against node-local storage** — shards never cross nodes and are never duplicated. ~450 lines over `CPUOffloadingSpec`, loaded via the existing `spec_module_path` hook, no core changes beyond the per-group geometry in #54413.

Production numbers (2× NVIDIA DGX Spark, GB10 unified memory, GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 TP=2 with DFlash2 speculation): 155k-token session restored in 36.6 s vs 205 s recompute after a **full engine restart**; 10 *simultaneous* restores after restart, 10/10 needle-correct, TTFTs 18–164 s stacking gracefully.

Production deployment of GLM 5.1 FP8 on TP=8 + PP=2 across two nodes hangs deterministically the moment any request includes `logprobs:true`. The same prompt without logprobs returns in seconds. # [Bugfix][DCP] Fix NVIDIA DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2 fused attention

Fixes #50095.

## Purpose

Fix two DCP correctness defects in the fused DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.2
attention path:

- The fused norm/RoPE kernel skipped query RMSNorm when a DCP rank had no
  owner-local KV-cache slot. KV ownership does not remove that rank's query
  contribution.
- Pure DCP sent only rank-local query heads into attention over owner-local KV

  metadata; its sparse backend supplies neutral contributions for empty local
  shards.
- Extend the existing fused norm/RoPE test with an all-negative-slot regression

items.title: Add MoNe experts pruning support
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Mixture of Novices and Experts (MoNe) is an expert pruning method accepted at ICLR-2026 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.00390
 
The method computes statistics (access frequency and output variance) about experts during calibration, identifies redundant experts and replaces them with constant vectors which are their unbiased estimators. MoNe is planned to be supported in the llm-compressor https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/2906 

Given MoNe replaces redundant expert's MLP blocks with constant vectors, it requires custom support in vllm. 

This PR is the first self-contained step toward broader MoNE support. It introduces an algorithm-independent expert-substitution checkpoint contract and implements the minimal constant-v1 inference path for unquantized DeepSeek/GLM models using the Triton backend and tensor parallelism. It intentionally does not support additional model families, replacement formats, quantized experts, expert/data parallelism, or other MoE backends.

## Purpose

**This is a broad, real-model-triggerable correctness fix for
`persistent_topk`: candidate-buffer overflow can silently degrade attention
accuracy, and the fix introduces no material performance regression in the
measured kernel and end-to-end workloads.**

Fixes #51782.

**Impact:** This is not limited to synthetic logits. It reproduced end to end
on stock vLLM v0.27.0 with `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`
(`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `index_topk=2048`). A real 134,249-token
MRCR 2-needle prompt submitted as 33 sequences dispatched

silently returned wrong top-k values in up to 27/33 rows, with up to
2,042/2,048 wrong selected values in one row and a maximum score delta of
6.5967. Replaying the same six captured runtime tensors through this PR three
times each produced zero mismatches. Longer contexts make overflow increasingly

items.title: [Bugfix][Parser] Terminate streamed tool arguments the flush cannot extend
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

A streaming tool call can end with `finish_reason` set while `arguments` is cut off mid-string. Any client that calls `json.loads` on the accumulated arguments fails on it. Reproduced live on Qwen3.8-27B in 7 of 25 requests sent straight at the worker, no proxy in the path.

`_safe_arg_prefix` (`parser_engine.py:283`) deliberately streams unterminated string values for prefix-stable keys. Its own docstring carries the contract: "String values for keys in `string_keys` are prefix-stable, so stream their unterminated content instead of buffering long arguments until the closing tag arrives." Something has to close them, and that something is the flush.

`_flush_arg_converter` (`parser_engine.py:963`) re-derives the arguments with `partial=False`. Every in-tree `arg_converter` builds its result from completed parameters and folds the still-open one in under `if partial:`. So when generation ends while a parameter is open, the non-partial re-derivation **drops that parameter**, and the result is neither longer than nor a prefix of what was already streamed. Both guards fail, the function returns `None`, and nothing ever terminates the prefix the client is holding.

This is not conditional on the model misbehaving. Anything that ends generation with a parameter open reaches it: a `max_tokens` stop, a stop string, or a malformed continuation.

### Blast radius, measured

Each converter called directly with one complete parameter and one open parameter:

items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Bound the decode paged-MQA-logits sanitize to the top-k read region
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

After [vllm#49714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49714), every decode step runs `nan_to_num_(-inf)` over the full
`[rows, max_model_len]` logits workspace. On GLM-5.2 `max_model_len` is 258048,
so this costs 43 us per call regardless of how short the context is.

The top-k only reads the front of each row. This PR sanitizes just that slice
using a small Triton kernel, and falls back to `nan_to_num_` below 10M elements
where a kernel launch isn't worth it.

## Safety

- The sanitized region is a superset of what the top-k reads, so the result is
  identical.
- NaN/Inf handling matches `nan_to_num_(-inf)` exactly: NaN -> `-inf`,
  `+inf` -> `FLT_MAX`, `-inf` -> `-FLT_MAX`.
- The launch grid depends only on the row count (a shape), so CUDA graph capture
  stays valid.

## Results

MI355X TP=4, ISL 1024 / OSL 256 / concurrency 256. Same image, same bench
arguments, with and without this commit.

One decode step, rank 0. Both panels show the same 130 us window:

![decode-step timeline, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amd-sriram/vllm/f87421d965c40b2d39e1cdbf1e4b5acac23348ff/figures/fig_pr7_timeline.png)

The sanitize sits between `paged_mqa_logits` and the top-k. Before: 44.4 us.
After: 4.6 us.

Over the whole run, rank 0:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| sanitize launches | 9,885 | 9,870 |
| avg per call | 43.13 us | 4.59 us |
| total GPU time | 426.3 ms | **51.9 ms** |
| % of GPU kernel time | 1.82% | **0.21%** |

Same launch count, each call does less work. Rank 1 matches (427 ms -> 50 ms).

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Normalize null assistant content with tool_calls
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

- Normalize assistant messages with `content: null` and `tool_calls` to use an empty string before chat templating.
- Prevents Jinja templates that render `{{ content }}` from injecting the literal string `None` into the prompt.
- Adds regression coverage in `test_chat_utils.py`.

## Problem

OpenAI agent clients (OpenAI SDK, pi, etc.) commonly send assistant turns as `content: null` plus `tool_calls`. When those messages reach `apply_chat_template`, templates that unconditionally render assistant content emit `None` as text. Over many tool-calling turns in an agent session, this silently degrades generation into repetition loops and looks like a model quality issue rather than a preprocessing bug.

Reported in #54337 with reproduction on GLM chat templates; the fix is protocol-layer and model-agnostic.

## Fix

Extend `_postprocess_messages` in `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py` to coerce `content=None` to `""` for assistant messages that include `tool_calls`, alongside the existing tool-call argument normalization.

## Test plan

- [x] Smoke-tested `_postprocess_messages` locally (null content becomes `""`, arguments still parsed)

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Guard GLMGA video sampling against zero source fps
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Motivation

`GLMGAVideoBackend.compute_frames_index_to_sample` divides by `source.original_fps` in two places — the duration fallback (`round(max_frame_idx / original_fps) + 1`) and `duration_per_frame = 1 / original_fps` — without validating it. vLLM reports `original_fps == 0` for clips with an unknown or variable frame rate (VFR, malformed containers, failed webcam captures), so those inputs crash with a bare `ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero`.

Every other fps-driven backend in `vllm/multimodal/video.py` already guards this (`Qwen2VLVideoBackend`, `Qwen3VLVideoBackend`, `GLM46VVideoBackend`, and `Molmo2VideoBackend` in fps mode); GLMGA is the remaining one without the check.

## Modifications

- Added the same `original_fps <= 0` guard to `GLMGAVideoBackend`, raising a descriptive `ValueError` that names the backend and the cause, mirroring the existing Qwen2-VL / Qwen3-VL behavior.
- Added a regression test covering both crash paths (duration reported vs. duration missing).

## Verification

- `pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py::test_glmga_video_backend_rejects_unknown_source_fps` -> 1 passed.
- On unpatched `main`, the same test fails with `ZeroDivisionError: float division by zero` for both `duration=5.0` (at `duration_per_frame = 1 / original_fps`) and `duration=0.0` (at the duration fallback).
- Neighbor sampling tests `pytest tests/multimodal/test_video.py -k glm46v`: 12 passed; the single failure (`test_video_processor_from_model_repo[glm46v]`) is an unrelated missing `av` module in my local environment and fails identically on unpatched `main`.

## Duplicate check

Searched open PRs and issues for `glmga`, `glmga fps`, and `video original_fps`: nothing covers the GLMGA backend. #53844 fixes the same bug class for `Qwen3VLVideoBackend` only and does not touch GLMGA; this PR is scoped to GLMGA so the two can land independently.

This change was developed with AI assistance (bug identification, patch, and regression test).

items.title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix BLHNC addressing for FlashInfer sparse MLA
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fix sparse MLA cache addressing when `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` uses a block-outermost KV-cache layout such as BLHNC.

BLHNC places other layers' pages between consecutive blocks of a given layer. Two paths incorrectly assumed that a layer's physical block stride was exactly its logical block size:

- FlashInfer sparse index conversion multiplied the physical block ID by `block_size`, causing decode to read another layer's page.
- The fused DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM cache writer derived the logical block size from the physical block stride, causing writes to land in the wrong block or layer.

## Changes

- Derive the physical row stride from the actual FlashInfer KV-cache view and pass it through both regular and DCP sparse-index conversion.
- Pass the logical MLA block size explicitly to the fused cache writer.
- Extend DCP physical-remapping coverage to a non-dense block stride.

This change allows a TP1 PCP producer whose DCP group spans the PCP group to transfer its distinct DCP KV shards to a consumer with the same DCP size. Replicated PCP behavior remains unchanged.
